crowd_vs_news.news_narrative: Evercore downgraded Reddit and Google AI-search summaries are killing referral traffic and user growth.
crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Users see the selloff as an overreaction and are underwriting a near-term OpenAI data-licensing deal worth $1B+/year that offsets referral losses.
crowd_vs_news.who_is_right: The crowd has a real point that data licensing is a genuine offset, but the $1B/year figure is speculative and the OpenAI deal is unconfirmed. Evercore's traffic concern is the more concrete near-term risk; the licensing upside is optionality, not a base case.

crowd_vs_news.news_narrative: Intel plunged ~29% on weak PC outlook and a Goldman target cut; the AI trade is unwinding.
crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Users call it manipulation and naked shorting, cite a pre-earnings Israel fab fire, and are buying the dip as a 'once in 52 year' chance.
crowd_vs_news.who_is_right: The fundamental guidance cut is real and the market reaction is largely justified; the naked-shorting and fire claims are unverified retail grievance. The dip-buyers are catching a falling knife until PC demand stabilizes.

crowd_vs_news.news_narrative: Alphabet had its worst week in ~15 years as AI capex fears and a brutal selloff hit the stock.
crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Users point to RSI ~21, an S&P-10 name at a 31% drawdown, and are loading calls/stock for a bounce; some flag the buyback halt and ATM issuance as a real negative.
crowd_vs_news.who_is_right: The buyback-halt/ATM point is the sharpest bearish detail and is underappreciated. But an RSI-21 bounce trade is a tactical call, not a thesis; the negative-FCF and halted-buyback mechanics argue the de-rating has fundamental legs.

crowd_vs_news.news_narrative: Precigen cratered 27% after-hours because rival Inovio's rare-disease drug got FDA approval.
crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Bulls say PGEN's first-to-market payer/J-code lock-in protects it and Inovio is underfunded and will dilute; bears say Voceryq makes Papzimeos obsolete within 60 days.
crowd_vs_news.who_is_right: Both sides have a real mechanism. First-to-market plus payer setup is a durable moat, but clinical superiority that avoids repeat surgeries is a genuine threat. The Nov 4 earnings and launch numbers will settle it; the 27% drop looks like an overreaction but not a clean buy until payer uptake is visible.

RDDT.summary: Reddit (RDDT) is the most-discussed stock on Reddit's own platform over the past 24 hours, with mentions jumping from 269 to 351 and ranking #1. The conversation is overwhelmingly bullish on Stocktwits (12 bullish vs. 4 bearish tags), and the message board reads like a mix of dip-buying bravado and speculation about AI data licensing deals. One user proudly dropped over $150k into the stock today despite being down a bit, mocking political narratives and betting on a one-year turnaround. Another points to a potential licensing deal with OpenAI that could send shares back to the $130–140 range 'in a heartbeat.' The core bull case centers on Reddit's valuable user-generated data: with access to data now limited, LLMs need to pay up, and several posters believe data licensing deals could bring in at least $1 billion per year, more than offsetting any loss from Google referrals. There's also chatter about Tom Lee's comment that the market is acting like someone got liquidated, drawing parallels to a prior liquidation event. On the bear side, the stock is being compared unfavorably to Snap, with one quip: 'SNAP: I'm the worst stock ever! RDDT: Hold my beer.' Another poster sarcastically notes that stocks are never overvalued and only go up, highlighting risk-management concerns. The overall tone is defiantly optimistic, with investors viewing the selloff as a 'mega opportunity' to buy. However, the heavy retail enthusiasm and political undertones suggest a speculative frenzy that could cut both ways. Investors should watch for concrete news on AI licensing partnerships and any updates on Google referral traffic, as those are the key swing factors. The stock's high mention volume and bullish tilt indicate strong retail conviction, but also raise contrarian concerns about crowded positioning.

INTC.summary: Intel (INTC) is the second most-mentioned stock on Reddit over the past 24 hours, with mentions rising from 145 to 201. The discussion is more balanced than Reddit's overall bullish tilt, with Stocktwits showing 16 bullish tags versus 11 bearish. The conversation is dominated by dip-buying enthusiasm after a sharp selloff—one poster calls it a 'once in 52 year chance' and opened a new position, while another sold at $101 but still loves the company. Several users express confidence in buying the dip, with one saying 'I feel really good about buying in today and going Long' and another expecting a bounce by Monday. However, there's also a strong undercurrent of frustration and conspiracy: one poster claims 'more naked shorting, more price spoofing, more failing to delivers' and rants about PC and memory shortages that were supposedly predicted two earnings ago. Another criticizes a bearish playbook that has seen Intel drop 30% while Alibaba only fell 1.5%, highlighting the stock's underperformance. The bearish case centers on Intel's steep decline, with one user simply posting 'Damn!' and a bearish tag. The overall tone is cautiously optimistic, with bulls viewing the selloff as an overreaction and bears pointing to structural issues. Investors should note that Intel's turnaround story remains uncertain, and the stock's high volatility is attracting both value seekers and short-term traders. The heavy mention volume suggests retail interest is elevated, which can amplify moves in either direction.

GOOG.summary:
Alphabet (GOOG/GOOGL) is getting a lot of attention in online communities, though the conversation has cooled from a recent peak. Reddit mentions dropped sharply from 476 to 152 in the last 24 hours, but the stock still ranks 5th most-discussed. On Stocktwits, sentiment is clearly bullish, with 21 bullish tags versus only 5 bearish. The chatter is a mix of technical, fundamental, and even space-related excitement.

A big driver is the recent earnings report. One popular post highlights the CEO's comments: Q3 revenue run rate is now half a trillion dollars annually, with Alphabet growing at 25%. Management says AI investments are boosting Search query growth, including commercial queries, and year-over-year query growth is the highest in five years. That's a strong signal that Google's core business remains healthy and AI isn't cannibalizing search as some feared. Investors are also noting the stock's low RSI of 21, which technically suggests it's oversold and due for a bounce. One user bluntly said, "When an S&P10 company is at an RSI of 21, you f***in buy." Others are accumulating shares, with one mentioning a $25K purchase.

There's also buzz about Project Suncatcher, Google's moonshot to put TPUs in orbit. A post describes how ground controllers successfully sent a command to a satellite, booted up an onboard TPU, ran an AI model (Gemma), and downlinked the response. While this is a long-term speculative project, it adds to the narrative that Google is pushing the boundaries of AI and cloud computing.

On the bearish side, some worry about the broader AI trade and potential risks to Google's ad business. However, the overall tone is optimistic. Many see the recent pullback as a buying opportunity, especially given the strong fundamentals. The drop in Reddit mentions could simply mean the stock is less controversial now, or that retail attention has shifted elsewhere. Still, the Stocktwits crowd remains firmly in the bull camp, expecting a climb in the coming days. Investors should watch for continued AI progress, ad market trends, and any regulatory headwinds, but for now, the community sees more upside than downside.

AMD.summary:
AMD is buzzing on social media, with Reddit mentions skyrocketing from 37 to 142 in the last 24 hours, putting it at rank 6. Stocktwits sentiment is strongly bullish, with 22 bullish tags versus 6 bearish. The conversation is a mix of optimism about upcoming earnings, dip-buying enthusiasm, and comparisons to rivals like Intel and Nvidia.

A major theme is the recent price drop. AMD shares fell about 13% in a short period, which many see as an overreaction. One popular post noted that the drop was due to Intel's issues and broader market weakness ahead of earnings, and predicted AMD will "fly on earnings." Others are buying the dip, with comments like "Congrats to all that bought at 50-70 discount" and expectations of a rebound to $580-600 next week. The bullish case is built on AMD's strong product lineup, especially in AI chips, and the belief that the company is fundamentally different from Intel.

Investors are also discussing AMD's heavy investment in next-generation chips. A post pointed out that sometimes the spending Wall Street complains about today builds competitive advantage tomorrow, comparing AMD to Amazon and Netflix. This reflects confidence in management's long-term vision. The recent buy volume spike at the close was interpreted as a bullish signal, with one user saying shorts got "punked."

However, there are concerns. The broader semiconductor sector has been weak, with stocks like AAOI, SNDK, COHR, and Dell also down double digits. Some worry that AMD's valuation is stretched and that competition from Nvidia remains fierce. Intel's troubles could spill over, and the AI trade might be cooling. Still, the dominant sentiment is that AMD is a buying opportunity, especially with earnings on the horizon. The community expects a strong report and a subsequent rally. Investors should watch for guidance on AI chip demand and data center growth, as these are key drivers. Overall, the online crowd is betting on a comeback.

NVDA.summary: Nvidia is once again the center of attention in online investing communities, with Reddit mentions nearly tripling from 38 to 107 in the past 24 hours, pushing it to rank 7 among all tickers discussed. On Stocktwits, the mood is overwhelmingly bullish, with 27 bullish tags versus only 4 bearish ones. The message board reads like a mix of dip-buying celebration and AI optimism. One popular post congratulates everyone who 'grabbed the dip' and looks forward to the weekend, while another insists 'there is no AI bubble' because TSMC can't meet demand and Nvidia's earnings are set to skyrocket. There's also a fair amount of short-term trading chatter, like the user who bought $10k on the dip and made a quick $75 by luck, or the one who bought 6,000 shares and declared 'we can go up now.' Investors should note that while sentiment is very positive, much of the discussion is anecdotal and momentum-driven. The AI narrative remains the core bullish thesis, but any negative surprise in earnings or guidance could quickly shift the mood. Also, the high level of bullish tags on Stocktwits can sometimes be a contrarian indicator when it gets too extreme. Overall, the community sees Nvidia as a must-own AI leader and is using dips as buying opportunities, but the chatter is light on deep fundamental analysis and heavy on short-term trading psychology.

TSLA.summary: Tesla is getting a lot of attention online right now, with Reddit mentions more than doubling in the past 24 hours to 83, putting it at rank 9 among all stocks. On Stocktwits, the bullish sentiment is clearly ahead, with 15 bullish tags versus 6 bearish ones. But if you dig into the actual messages, a lot of the chatter isn't really about Tesla's cars or financials—it's about Elon Musk. Many posts are political rants, jokes about Musk's personal life, or references to SpaceX (ticker $SPCX) and other unrelated topics. For example, one popular post talks about "socialists destroy countries" and tags Tesla, while another mentions Elon wanting to go to Epstein's island. This kind of noise can make it hard to find real analysis. Still, there are some genuine bullish calls: one user says "$TSLA 450 soon merger done," and another posts a recap of successful options trades, including Tesla puts and calls with big gains. The overall vibe is mixed but leans positive, with a lot of speculative energy. Investors should be aware that much of the discussion is driven by Musk's polarizing persona and political comments rather than fundamentals. The stock is often grouped with $SPY, $QQQ, and $SPCX in posts, suggesting people are trading it as part of broader market or tech plays. There's also some frustration about Musk's political attacks on Democrats, which could turn off some investors. On the positive side, the high mention volume and bullish tags indicate strong retail interest, and options traders are actively betting on both directions. But the lack of substantive company-specific news in the chatter means you should be cautious about reading too much into the sentiment. Tesla remains a volatile stock, and the online community is clearly divided, with passionate bulls and bears. Keep an eye on any actual news about vehicle deliveries, margins, or Musk's other ventures, as those will likely drive the stock more than the daily noise.

The stock is often mentioned alongside other tech giants like Nvidia and Google, and some see it as a buying opportunity. Keep in mind that Amazon's massive spending on AI and AWS is a double-edged sword—it could pay off big, but it also weighs on margins. The community seems to believe that the stock is ready to run, especially if the broader market stabilizes after the midterms.

PGEN.summary: Precigen (PGEN) is getting a lot of buzz on Stocktwits, mostly because of its connection to INO (Inovio). The FDA recently green-lit Inovio's CELLECTRA 5PSP delivery device, which is used with DNA medicines. PGEN itself isn't the one with the approval, but traders are excited because PGEN is seen as a pure-play DNA medicines company with a similar technology. Many are calling PGEN a 'monopoly' with record revenues and profits, and they think the market is overreacting to INO's news. Some are loading up on shares, expecting a short squeeze similar to what happened with INO. The sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish: 23 bullish tags versus just 1 bearish tag. However, there are no Reddit mentions in the last 24 hours, so the discussion is concentrated on Stocktwits. Investors should note that PGEN is a small-cap biotech with no direct FDA approval news of its own. The excitement is largely sympathy-driven, and the stock could be volatile. While the company has revenue from its portfolio, it's not clear how much of the bullishness is justified by fundamentals versus hype. The mention of 'record revenues and profits' is a positive, but biotech investments carry high risk. The lack of Reddit chatter might indicate limited broader interest, so the rally could be short-lived. Overall, the community is very optimistic, but investors should do their own due diligence and not get caught up in the hype.

LLY.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) is a hot topic on both Reddit and Stocktwits, with 11 Reddit mentions in the last 24 hours (up from 8) and a Reddit rank of 44. The Stocktwits sentiment is mostly bullish (22 bullish vs 4 bearish tags). The discussion revolves around LLY's massive market cap (over $1.3 trillion), its weight-loss and diabetes drugs, and its position as a leader in biotech. Some users are joking about short sellers who bet against LLY at $900, while others are waiting for a stock split. There's also chatter about LLY's involvement in bidding for Metsera (a private company) and its potential in the obesity market. Elon Musk's mention of LLY (and TZP) has sparked some interest, with users suggesting he should also look at VKTX. Overall, the community sees LLY as a strong, profitable company with a bright future, but some express concerns about valuation and the possibility of a pullback. Investors should know that LLY is a large-cap pharma giant with a diversified portfolio, but its stock is sensitive to drug trial results, regulatory decisions, and competition in the GLP-1 space. The bullishness is driven by its earnings power and pipeline, but the high valuation leaves little room for error. The Reddit and Stocktwits activity suggests retail investors are actively trading LLY, which could add volatility. While the long-term outlook is positive, short-term fluctuations are likely. Overall, the community is confident in LLY's fundamentals but mindful of its premium price.

TTWO.summary: Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) is getting a lot of love on Stocktwits right now, with 25 bullish tags versus just 2 bearish ones. The Reddit crowd is completely silent—zero mentions in the last 24 hours—so this is purely a Stocktwits party. The vibe is overwhelmingly positive, almost giddy. One user compared TTWO to Tesla at $225, saying adults underestimate how popular the company's games are, especially the live-service stuff where players keep spending on skins and virtual currency. Another joked about moving money from their bank account to buy more shares. Several are buying the dip, noting the stock is down about 28% from its highs and heading into Q2 earnings on November 9th. There's also chatter about the stock's setup looking like the end of March, which was apparently a bottom. Some are just frustrated by the volatility—'roller coaster of emotions' and 'playing with my emotions'—but even they seem to be holding. The main driver is clearly Grand Theft Auto, likely GTA VI hype, which users say is bigger than any movie ever released. The live-service angle is a big deal too: recurring revenue from virtual currency and online modes gives the stock a subscription-like feel. Investors should know that sentiment is extremely bullish, which can sometimes be a contrarian signal, but the fundamentals around GTA VI and live services are strong. Earnings on Nov 9th is the next catalyst. The stock's recent drop might be a buying opportunity, but keep in mind the community is very one-sided, so any disappointment could hit hard. Overall, the discussion is optimistic, with users encouraging others to buy the dip and hold for the long term.
